meta.title: Expert-labeled analog pairs (training labels)
meta.description: Each row is a published-literature-informed expert similarity judgment between one Earth candidate site and one Moon/Mars target, on a 0-1 scale. The model learns feature weights from these labels via ridge regression (pairwise-labels approach), so every label needs a rationale. Scores deliberately encode 'where the analogy breaks down' — e.g., an Atacama site remains a strong Mars analog despite Earth-level atmosphere.
meta.scale: 0 = no meaningful analogy, 0.5 = moderate (shares 1-2 strong dimensions), 0.75+ = strong multi-dimensional analog, 1.0 = canonical benchmark

pairs.rationale: Canonical Mars soil analog: perchlorate-bearing, organic-depleted soils under hyperaridity; atmosphere/gravity remain the breakdown.
Dry-limit soils used to calibrate life-detection; strongest aridity analog in the catalog.
Acid-sulfate brines and iron-oxide terraces mirror Meridiani-type alteration; habitability-edge process analog despite extreme heat.
Published Mars analog: yardangs + sulfates + hyperaridity at altitude; terrain-process match is strong.
Hottest measured land surface plus yardang province — thermal and aeolian-process analog.
Process-only analog: world's largest dust source vs martian dust storms; geology does not match.
Full dune-type inventory (star/linear/barchan) matches Bagnold-dune morphology classes.
Compact barchan field analog for martian dunes and granular-mobility testing.
Dust-lifting and storm-propagation process analog; otherwise dissimilar geology.
Cold high-altitude desert with permafrost, springs and rover trials — multi-dimensional ISRO Mars analog.
Permafrost polygons and ground ice mirror Utopia's polygonal patterned ground.
Benchmark cold-desert permafrost analog; canonical but retained as calibration.
High-altitude UV and salars approximate early-Mars surface chemistry; moderate overall.
Dust devils + hydrothermal sinter under high UV; thermal springs are the mismatch.
Olivine-rich crust with serpentinization habitability — matches Jezero's mafic-floor mineralogy.
Subsurface H2-driven habitability analog in mafic crust.
Active basaltic shield volcanism process analog for Tharsis; no preserved tubes.
Fissure-fed basalt plains with tubes and ash zones; Russian planetary training analog.
Vast young basalt field used for Mars-mission field exercises.
The strongest lava-tube/skylight analog in the catalog; ESA PANGAEA training site.
Cave + meteorite-surface operations analog; geology mismatch for mare basalt.
Thermal-extreme, below-sea-level arid basin analog.
Small crater + evaporite floor combination; volcanic genesis is the mismatch.
Evaporite crust polygon analog; otherwise wet and flat.
Large-scale evaporite terrain analog for martian chloride/sulfate regions.
Only Earth impact crater in flood basalt — the closest analog for craters in mare crust (ISRO lunar analog).
Benchmark fresh simple-crater morphology; Apollo-era training site.
Young simple crater in hard basement rock, crisp rim/ejecta.
Well-preserved simple crater interacting with dune sediments.
Deeply eroded complex-crater ring — analog for degraded ancient craters, not fresh morphology.
Impact into loose sand = regolith-crater formation process analog at small scale.
Basalt plains + lava tubes; Apollo-era NASA analog for mare-plains operations.
Flood-basalt plains analog for maria; weathering/vegetation reduce the match.
Basalt plateaus + deep canyon walls; permafrost cover mutes the match.
Large intact lava tube — interior microenvironment analog for Kaguya skylight target.
Apollo-trained volcanic field; caldera/rille-like volcanic landforms.
Apollo 15-era Iceland training context; volcanic collapse structures.
Polar impact-crater operations analog; thermal cycle far milder than lunar PSRs.
Cryogenic sample-recovery process analog; not a landform analog.
Impact crater partially buried by dunes — degradation-process analog.
Sealed chemosynthetic subsurface ecosystem — habitability-inside-caves analog.
Olivine lithology matches mare basalts; tectonic setting does not.
Bright high-albedo dunes and dust devils; gypsum chemistry is the mismatch.
Official Apollo 17 training crater with olivine-bearing xenoliths.
Weak: aridity helps, but lunar thermal cycle/vacuum dominate the mismatch.
Mars-like yardangs + sulfates + cold winters — a strong all-round Mars analog.
Playa desiccation analog for paleolake floors; biology and rainfall present.
